checks: qorbanot_bar_kappara.xml:34: the quotation seg's source is now urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:leviticus/2/11/b. In JLPTEI-3 'Sub-verse scope', b means the next word after the etnachta through the end of the verse. In Lev 2:11 the etnachta falls on חָמֵץ, so b is exactly 'כִּי כָל־שְׂאֹר … אִשֶּׁה לַיהוָה', the words quoted. The source goes on a bounded seg and not a corresp, so no canonical verse identity is claimed or duplicated. If a cited Tanakh project has no half-verses, the reference falls back to the whole verse and the compiler logs it, as the spec intends. My earlier finding is resolved.

machzor_expanded index.xml:1392-1415: the Shabbat conditional (shabbat=true) now wraps a tei:div. Inside it, j:declare section_morning_qorbanot_shabbat_settings (shabbat=true), the musaf/shabbat transclusion and the matching j:endDeclare are siblings, which meets the sibling rule for declare/endDeclare. j:conditional and j:endConditional are siblings in the outer div. The declaration has the same value as the gate, so the 'kind of day' gating on the declaration can't change the result. This follows 'Conditions on a running order'. The bilingual 'בשבת:'/'On Shabbat:' instruction note is right here: this is an in-section condition rubric under 'Kinds of rubric', not a whole-section gate. My earlier finding is resolved.

Partial chapter @n without @corresp: resolutions.json:30 and :38 now record it as a context-only number. That matches the schema. I accept this as a project convention. I did not reopen the earlier accepted modules to confirm they encode it the same way.

findings.issue: My round-1 claim that the line 'clearly ends עַל־' was made at band resolution, and I withdraw it. In the isolated crop the margin to the left of the lamed is blank, so there is no detached maqaf. The lamed's horizontal waist stroke does run about 80px (crop scale) to the left of where the ascender meets it, at the top-of-letter height where a maqaf would sit, and it ends in a slight blob. That overhang is almost certainly what I read as a maqaf. This crop alone can't show whether it is the typeface's lamed form or a maqaf fused to the lamed by scan blur.
findings.recommendation: Keep the space provisionally. Do not require the maqaf. Send it to the human with this snippet plus a line-internal lamed from the same page (e.g. שֶׁלִּזְבָחִים or עַל־מִזְבַּח in Mishnah 1) for comparison. Add it to pending_human_questions in resolutions.json, which doesn't list it yet.
